origin.description: Pointwise and overall confidence envelopes for a curve evaluated at fixed abscissae.
origin.usage: envelope(boot.out = NULL, mat = NULL, level = 0.95, index = 1:ncol(mat))

arguments.name: boot.out
arguments.text: A bootstrap object whose t matrix holds the curve at fixed points. If t is a matrix it replaces mat.

arguments.name: mat
arguments.text: Matrix of bootstrap replicates, one row per replicate and one column per abscissa. Required when boot.out does not supply a matrix.

arguments.name: level
arguments.text: Confidence level. A single value is used for both envelopes. A pair gives the pointwise level and then the overall level.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based columns of mat that belong to the curve. At least two columns are required.

origin.details: The pointwise envelope is a pair of order statistics in each column. Its overall error is the proportion of replicates that fall outside the envelope somewhere, divided by R+1. Further order statistics are tried until the overall error is about 1 - level[2]. If even the extreme envelope is too wide for that error, a warning is given and the extremes are returned. The manual example draws the envelopes on a normal QQ plot of gravity series 8. The captured example prints the envelope and draws the same four lines on a fixed curve.
origin.value: A list with point and overall (two rows each, upper then lower), k.pt and k.ov (the order-statistic positions), err.pt and err.ov (pointwise error and overall error of that envelope), and err.nom (the nominal errors 1 - level).
origin.example:
mat <- outer(1:80, 1:5, function(a, b) (a * b) %% 17 + b)
ev <- envelope(mat = mat, level = c(0.8, 0.95))
print(ev)
xs <- seq_len(ncol(mat))
plot(xs, ev$point[1, ], type = "l", lty = 2,
     ylim = range(ev$point, ev$overall),
     xlab = "point", ylab = "envelope")
lines(xs, ev$point[2, ], lty = 2)
lines(xs, ev$overall[1, ], lty = 1)
lines(xs, ev$overall[2, ], lty = 1)

translation.description: Pointwise and overall confidence envelopes for a curve evaluated at fixed abscissae.

arguments.name: boot_out
arguments.text: An object whose t attribute is a two-dimensional array of curve replicates. If so, it replaces mat.

arguments.name: mat
arguments.text: Array of bootstrap replicates, one row per replicate and one column per abscissa. Required when boot_out does not supply a matrix.

arguments.name: level
arguments.text: Confidence level. A single value is used for both envelopes. A pair gives the pointwise level and then the overall level.

arguments.name: index
arguments.text: 1-based columns that belong to the curve. None uses every column. At least two columns are required.

translation.details: The pointwise envelope is a pair of order statistics in each column. Ranks use the average of tied positions. The overall error counts replicates whose ranks leave the envelope in any column, divided by R+1. The search walks integer order statistics until the overall error sits next to the requested level. If the extreme envelope cannot reach that error, a warning is given and the extremes are returned. The four envelope lines are drawn with Matplotlib.
translation.value: A namespace with point and overall (shape (2, p), upper then lower), k_pt and k_ov, err_pt and err_ov, and err_nom.
translation.example:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from boot.influence import envelope

mat = (np.arange(1, 81)[:, None] * np.arange(1, 6)[None, :]) % 17 + np.arange(1, 6)
ev = envelope(mat=mat, level=[0.8, 0.95])
print(ev.point)
print(ev.overall)
print(ev.k_pt)
print(ev.err_pt)
print(ev.k_ov)
print(ev.err_ov)
print(ev.err_nom)
xs = np.arange(1, mat.shape[1] + 1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(xs, ev.point[0], linestyle="--")
ax.plot(xs, ev.point[1], linestyle="--")
ax.plot(xs, ev.overall[0], linestyle="-")
ax.plot(xs, ev.overall[1], linestyle="-")
ax.set_xlabel("point")
ax.set_ylabel("envelope")
